newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Caemi denies acquisition talks.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Caemi denies acquisition talks.

text.p: Brazil's largest private mining company Caemi denied press reports that it would be sold to foreign mining firms RTZ Corp Plc and Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd.

In a statement sent to the local bolsas, Caemi said the press reports were incorrect, according to an official at Caemi Mineracao e Metalurgia's market relations department, who asked not to be named.
RTZ Corp Brazilian unit, RTZ Mineracao, has also denied it was negotiating with Anglo American Corp of South Africa the purchase of Caemi.
"These stories are improper," said RTZ's unit financial director Julio Carvalho.

On Monday, Caemi preferred shares climbed 16.66 percent to 49 reais on speculative trade after local weekly magazine Veja said Caemi would be acquired by the two foreign mining companies. According to Veja, Caemi would be sold because of succession problems triggered by the death of its founder late last year.
Veja said RTZ would take over Caemi's iron ore operations while Anglo American would buy the company's kaolin, bauxite and chromite businesses.
Caemi revenues in 1995 reached $524 million, with iron ore mining accounting for 75 percent of its total revenues, a company spokeswoman said.
